extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and structural/compactness results for ancient κ-solutions of the Ricci flow (definitions, point-picking lemmas, neck/bump criteria, and the asymptotic shrinking-solition convergence). Focus is on geometric/curvature conditions used to select scales, extract limits, and deduce splitting or soliton structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancient κ-solution (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A solution to the Ricci flow which is complete (either compact or noncompact), defined on an ancient time interval (−∞, T) with T > 0, has nonnegative curvature operator and bounded curvature, and is κ-noncollapsed on all scales for some positive constant κ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the class of solutions the chapter studies; the listed properties are the requirements one checks to classify a solution as an ancient κ-solution and to apply subsequent compactness, curvature, and structure theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: ε-neck of radius r (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An open subset N is an ε-neck of radius r if (N, r^{-2} g_{ij}) is ε-close, in the C^{[ε^{-1}]} topology, to a standard neck S^{n-1} × I, where S^{n-1} is the round (n−1)-sphere with scalar curvature 1 and I is an interval of length 2ε^{-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines a tubular/neck region at a given scale; quantitative closeness (ε, C^{[ε^{-1}]}) and the rescaling by r^{-2} are the precise criteria used to identify neck regions in curvature-scale analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neck radius lower bound (Proposition 6.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a positive constant ε0 = ε0(n) and r0 > 0 such that every ε-neck of radius r on a complete noncompact n-dimensional Riemannian manifold with nonnegative sectional curvature, with ε ≤ ε0, must have r ≥ r0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a quantitative obstruction: in nonnegative curvature manifolds, sufficiently accurate necks (small ε) cannot occur at arbitrarily small radii. Use to prevent arbitrarily small-scale neck degeneration at infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curvature β-bump and λ-remote (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A geodesic ball B(p,r) is a curvature β-bump if the sectional curvature K ≥ β / r^2 at all points in the ball. The ball B(p,r) is λ-remote from an origin O if d(p,O) ≥ λ r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions quantify localized high-curvature regions (bumps) and their remoteness from a chosen origin; they are the atomic objects counted/controlled in the finite bump theorem and in analyses of geometry at infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite Bump Theorem (Hamilton)
rubrics_metrics.description: For every β > 0 there exists λ < ∞ such that in any complete manifold of nonnegative sectional curvature there are at most a finite number of disjoint balls which are λ-remote curvature β-bumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A structural constraint used to control the number of disjoint, remote, high-curvature regions; used in arguments about singularity models at infinity and in dimension-reduction arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitting in scaling limit (Proposition 6.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (M, g_{ij}) is a complete n-dimensional manifold with nonnegative sectional curvature, P_k a sequence with λ_k > 0 and if the marked manifolds (M, λ_k^2 g_{ij}, P_k) converge in C^{∞}_{loc} to a limit and λ_k d(P, P_k) → ∞, then the limit splits isometrically as R × N (a product with a line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a criterion for when a blow-up (rescaling) limit contains a Euclidean line factor: large rescaled distance to a fixed basepoint forces splitting. It is used for dimension reduction and understanding asymptotic geometry of rescaled limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotic scalar curvature ratio A (diagnostic)
rubrics_metrics.description: A = lim sup_{s→∞} R s^2, where s is geodesic distance to a fixed origin and R is scalar curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A measures the growth rate of scalar curvature at infinity; A = +∞ triggers the point-picking lemma (6.1.3) to extract high-curvature regions/scales, while finite A leads to different analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-picking lemma for A = +∞ (Lemma 6.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a complete noncompact manifold with bounded curvature and asymptotic scalar curvature ratio A = +∞, one can find points x_j → ∞, radii r_j, and δ_j → 0 such that (i) R(x) ≤ (1 + δ_j) R(x_j) for all x in B(x_j, r_j), (ii) r_j^2 R(x_j) → ∞, (iii) λ_j := d(x_j,O)/r_j → ∞, and (iv) the balls B(x_j, r_j) are disjoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a constructive criterion for selecting near-maximal curvature centers on increasing scales whose scaled geometry can be studied independently; used to produce nontrivial blow-up limits at infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point selection in unbounded curvature case (Lemma 6.1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a complete noncompact manifold with unbounded curvature one can find x_j → ∞ with |Rm(x_j)| ≥ j and such that |Rm(x)| ≤ 4 |Rm(x_j)| for all x ∈ B(x_j, j / √|Rm(x_j)|).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a uniform control neighborhood around very high curvature points even when curvature is unbounded, allowing local rescalings and compactness arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Li–Yau–Perelman distance and estimates (l and reduced volume)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Li–Yau–Perelman distance l(q, τ) and reduced volume ˜V(τ) satisfy specific differential inequalities (e.g. (6.2.2)–(6.2.5)) including |∇ l|^2 + R ≤ 3 l / τ and evolution inequalities for l; also ˜V(τ) is monotone and bounded above by 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These analytic estimates are diagnostic criteria used to pick basepoints (minimizers of l), obtain scale-invariant control, derive gradient bounds, and apply Perelman's reduced-volume monotonicity in compactness and limit arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's reduced volume monotonicity (criterion for nonflat limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perelman's reduced volume ˜V(τ) is monotone nonincreasing under the Ricci flow and satisfies ˜V(τ) ≤ 1; equality ˜V ≡ 1 characterizes flat Euclidean space, so for nonflat ancient κ-solutions one has ˜V(τ) < 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect nonflatness of blow-up limits: if rescaled limits produced ˜V-limit strictly less than 1 then the limit cannot be flat, which is essential in proving convergence to a nonflat shrinking soliton.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotic shrinking soliton convergence (Theorem 6.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a nonflat ancient κ-solution there exist sequences of points q_k and times t_k → −∞ such that the scalings of g_{ij}(·, t) around q_k with factor |t_k|^{-1} and time shift converge in C^{∞}_{loc} to a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the operational criterion/result: by choosing minimizers q(τ) of l(·, τ), rescaling by τ^{-1}, using the Li–Yau–Perelman estimates, κ-noncollapsing, and reduced-volume monotonicity, one obtains convergence to a nonflat shrinking soliton. It prescribes the rescaling/selection procedure to extract the asymptotic soliton.
